programs.title: From Operators to Overseers: Infrastructure Careers and Worker Voice
programs.grade_or_level: Adult learners, apprentices and journeyworkers (e.g., operating engineers, electrical workers)
outcomes: Map how the six build-to-operate stages mirror real infrastructure trades work
Practice reading a steward-readable plan and flagging safety and handoff gaps
Draft a worker-voice checklist for when agents must hand incidents to people

sessions.activity: Compare a dam construction plan with a Planner-style build-and-run plan; identify decision points reserved for humans.
Walk the map's Intake Towers and Valve Houses as 'rehearsed provisioning'; discuss rehearsal-before-approval norms.
Role-play an on-call handoff: agent detects an anomaly, workers decide escalation and shutdown authority.
Discuss accountability: why registrations and spending stay human decisions even under automation.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized handoff-role-play transcripts and checklist items, tagged by trade and experience level, to a shared incident-handoff pattern library.
programs.consent: Adult learners sign a plain-language consent covering optional anonymized contributions; no names, employers, or site identifiers are retained, and anyone can opt out at any session.

programs.title: Build It, Run It: How Ideas Become Infrastructure
outcomes: Sequence the six stages from idea to operations using Hoover Dam's map features
Explain why some decisions (spending, votes, appointments) stay with people
Design a simple service plan and identify who checks it

sessions.activity: Sketch a plan for a school announcement service; trade plans for peer review like stewards reading a build plan.
Map scavenger hunt: match Intake Towers, spillways and powerhouse jobs to 'provisioning' steps on the map.
Paper-and-cards release exercise: build, release, and practice a rollback when a 'bug card' appears.
Gauges and logs: pretend-monitor the Exhibit Building displays and decide when to 'call a human.'

programs.data_shared: Anonymized plan sketches and decision-choice tallies (no names, ages, or writing samples) contributed to a shared model of how learners sequence build-to-operate stages.
programs.consent: Signed guardian/parent consent required before participation, plus student assent; all contributions are fully anonymized, schools may opt out of data sharing, and no personal data is collected.

programs.title: Governed Automation for Public-Interest Programs
programs.grade_or_level: Program staff and civic-technology leads, introductory
outcomes: Apply a six-zone model to a civic project lifecycle
Identify human-reserved decisions and design oversight checkpoints
Write a steward-readable plan for a small public service pilot

sessions.activity: Convert one real NGO program idea into a build-and-run plan with explicit human checkpoints.
Draft a secrets-handling policy exercise: what agents may touch, what only people approve.
Case discussion: why public-facing names and registrations are governance, not logistics.
Build an incident-handoff runbook template for community-facing services.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized plan templates and policy excerpts, stripped of organization and beneficiary details, contributed to a shared public-interest governance pattern library.
programs.consent: Organizational data-sharing agreement plus individual opt-in; contributions are reviewed for de-identification before inclusion, and communities discussed in plans are never identified.

programs.title: Nonprofit Stack Stewardship on a Mission Budget
programs.grade_or_level: Nonprofit operations and IT staff, beginner-friendly
outcomes: Understand the idea-to-production pipeline and where costs and approvals arise
Practice rollback thinking to protect service continuity
Define which tasks agents can rehearse and which need board or staff approval

sessions.activity: Prioritize one mission-critical service need and outline a minimal build-and-run plan.
Tabletop exercise: launch a donation-page update and rehearse a clean rollback when something breaks.
Set a secrets policy: who approves credentials, and how agents avoid handling live secrets.
Create a one-page on-call handoff sheet naming the human who decides during incidents.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized rollback-drill outcomes and handoff-sheet templates, with no donor, beneficiary, or organizational identifiers, added to a shared nonprofit resilience toolkit.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary with a simple opt-out; any shared artifacts are anonymized and reviewed by staff before submission, and no beneficiary or donor data is ever collected.
